common_name: Apple Teaser Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Series)

planting.note: Plant offsets or container starts in spring in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun; Apple Teaser is a Proven Winners Chick Charms introduction, a sport of 'Appletini'.

directions: Apple Teaser forms neat rosettes of apple-green leaves tipped and blushed with rosy red, intensifying in cooler weather and bright sun. Like other Chick Charms selections it multiplies readily by offsetting chicks around the mother rosette, quickly filling in a container or rock garden pocket. Grow in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun and avoid overwatering, since soggy conditions are the most common cause of rot in hardy sempervivums. Established clumps need little care beyond removing spent rosettes after they bloom and die back.

common_name: Strawberry Kiwi Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Series)

planting.note: Plant offsets or container starts in spring in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun; Strawberry Kiwi is a Proven Winners Chick Charms introduction with strong pink-and-green bicolor leaves.

directions: Strawberry Kiwi carries kiwi-green rosette centers that shade out to vivid strawberry-pink leaf tips, giving a bold two-tone effect that deepens with cold and bright sun exposure. It offsets freely into a tight mat of chicks, making it a reliable groundcover for rock gardens, green roofs, and container plantings. Grow in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun, and avoid wet, heavy soils that encourage rot. Remove spent mother rosettes after they flower and die back to keep the planting tidy.

common_name: Silver Suede Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Series)

planting.note: Plant offsets or container starts in spring in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun; Silver Suede is a Proven Winners Chick Charms introduction with a matte, silvery-gray rosette.

directions: Silver Suede forms tight, symmetrical rosettes in a soft, matte silver-gray with a suede-like texture, a cooler and more muted palette than many brighter Chick Charms siblings. It spreads by offsetting chicks that quickly fill gaps in a rock garden, trough, or mixed succulent container. Grow in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun; good drainage matters more than fertility for keeping this hardy succulent healthy through wet winters. Trim away spent rosettes after they bloom to keep the clump looking fresh.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in gritty, fast-draining succulent mix in full sun to bright partial shade; Gilva is a hybrid of E. agavoides and E. elegans.

directions: Gilva forms a tidy rosette of pale blue-green, slightly pointed leaves that take on pink to coral tones along the margins under bright light and cool temperatures. As an agavoides-elegans hybrid, it combines the thicker, more angular leaf shape of agavoides with the compact, pale coloring of elegans. Grow in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun to bright partial shade, and water only when the soil has dried out completely to avoid root and crown rot. Offsets form readily around the base and can be removed and rooted to propagate new plants.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in gritty, fast-draining succulent mix in full sun to bright partial shade.

directions: Muesli forms a compact, symmetrical rosette of slightly ruffled, speckled tan-and-green leaves, with coloring reminiscent of its namesake breakfast grain, especially when stressed by bright light or cooler temperatures. It is similar in form to Echeveria 'Imbricata' but carries its own distinct speckled leaf texture. Grow in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun to bright partial shade, and allow the soil to dry completely between waterings to prevent rot. Remove and root basal offsets to increase the planting.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in gritty, fast-draining succulent mix in full sun to bright partial shade; also sold under the trade name 'Conchita'.

directions: Agyntha forms a dense rosette of plump, pale blue-green leaves with a soft powdery bloom that rubs off easily, so it is best handled carefully or kept where it won't be brushed against. It clusters readily, forming a multi-headed mound over time as offsets form around the base. Grow in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun to bright partial shade, and water only after the soil has dried out completely to avoid rot. Protect from hard frost and overhead irrigation, which can mar the delicate leaf surface.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in gritty, fast-draining succulent mix in full sun to bright partial shade; firm, thick leaves make this selection unusually tolerant of brief dry spells.

directions: Martin's Hybrid carries the thick, firm, pointed leaves typical of Echeveria agavoides, colored pale green with red-tinged tips that intensify under strong sun and cool temperatures. The rosette holds a tighter, more architectural form than many softer Echeveria hybrids, giving it good structure in mixed succulent plantings. Grow in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun to bright partial shade, and let the soil dry fully between waterings to avoid rot. It tolerates brief dry spells better than thinner-leaved Echeveria types once established.
